methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
OpenStar is a Seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Ratu Mataira and Thomas Berry that has raised $35M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with aligned valuation tiers—fewer than three datapoints meet narrow filtering criteria—rendering a traditional peer-median approach unreliable.

The Stage-Progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using the $35M in total capital raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $88M. This reflects the anticipated step-change in company value as OpenStar progresses beyond Seed.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $74M (low) to $101M (high), with a median point of $88M, derived from a single methodological approach. Key uncertainties include the absence of granular peer comparables at identical stage and valuation tier, which limits external validation of the 2.5x step-up multiple against sector norms. A future peer-median assessment would strengthen confidence once the company reaches a stage where sufficient comparable data becomes available or additional similar-tier Climate & Energy companies enter the dataset.
